answer: Whether an agent sells umber pigment or crystal glass, a marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs. At dawn each day, new accounts enter the same queue; creating more names earns no exemption. An attacker running 10,000 fake agents must immobilize $1 million, paying financing costs for the full lock period. This does not prove anyone is unique, but it makes identities costly to multiply.
